name: Kam
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_citation: Lesage, Jakob. 2020. A grammar and lexicon of Kam (àŋwɔ̀m), a Niger-Congo language of central eastern Nigeria. PhD thesis, INALCO, Paris.https://theses.hal.science/tel-03004919/document
catalog_locator: ch. 4 'Prosodic prominence', §4.1.1-4.1.3 (thesis pp. 95-98); exceptions §4.3.1 Table 32 (p. 110) and §4.3.3 (pp. 112ff.)
catalog_quote: Prosodic strength is specified in the lexicon for every syllable, in a similar fashion that stress can be specified for every stem in some languages, and in a similar way that tonal patterns are also encoded for stems in Kam. ... Prosodic prominence is partly predictable from morphological structure. The first syllable with an onset is usually prosodically prominent in morphological stems, and most morphological stems feature just one prosodic stem. So, the prosodic stem of m̀pīɾī ‘goat’ is pīɾī, the prosodic stem of àlíb ‘head’ is líb, and the prosodic stem of káɾ ‘to accompany’ is simply káɾ. This system is in accordance with what has been found for many other languages in the Macro-Sudan belt (cf. § 1.1), where stem-initial prominence is identified as a salient areal phenomenon ... Prosodic prominence is not always predictable from the morphological structure of the lexeme alone, sin…

tone_statements.citation: Lesage, Jakob & Lora Litvinova. 2019. The tone system of Kam (Niger-Congo, Adamawa, Nigeria). Paper (slides) presented at the Adamawa Conference, Johannes Gutenberg-Universitaet Mainz, 9 September 2019. Slides posted by Adamawa Language Projects (Mainz) and the LLACAN AdaGram project.
tone_statements.quote: 4 Tone inventory • Surface contrast between three levels: L, M, and H • Contour tones: LH and HL ... • Notes on contrasts o Contours are combinations of L and H tones due to elision of a syllable o Contrasts with contours are difficult to find because ▪ LH is very rare (attested in 3 nouns) ▪ HL is rare (attested in 8 nouns) • M tones are fairly rare ... • Underlyingly, one could argue, Kam only has L and H tones. M tones are likely historically, and in some cases synchronically, derived from LH tones.
tone_statements.summary: Three surface levels L, M, H (M rare, arguably from LH, so underlyingly only L and H); contours LH/HL are L+H combinations from syllable elision; TBU = syllable; only floating L attested; floating L and delinked M cause downstep; H/M spread; replacive TAM tone; downdrift after L. Nothing on stress.

audit.reasoning: The record rests on the sole and authoritative description of Kam, a 622-page 2020 fieldwork-based reference grammar with a full chapter on prosodic prominence; we hold the PDF and the deciding quotation is verbatim at the cited pages (pp. 96-98, Table 32 p. 110, §4.3.3 p. 112). The classification (lexical prominence with a stem-initial default, pervasive lexical exceptions, no primary/secondary hierarchy, word/prosodic-stem domain) matches the author's own statements ('specified in the lexicon for every syllable'; 'partly predictable.. first syllable with an onset is usually prosodically prominent'; 'many exceptions'). No competing or newer stress/prosody source exists per Glottolog, HAL, ORCID, Crossref, LSP and the thesis's own survey of prior work (wordlists only before 2016). Nothing to add to the list of works to obtain; bibliographic query results

sources.citation: Lesage, Jakob. 2021. Stem initial accent and the phoneme inventory of Kam (Nigeria). Paper (slides) presented at the workshop 'Establishing phoneme inventories: argumentation and cross-linguistic comparability', International Conference of Nordic and General Linguistics (ICNGL), Oslo, 18 June 2021.
sources.note: Slides on a stem-initial non-tonal accent ('prosodic strength': length, loudness; 'Cf. Stress, but not really'). Tone presupposed, not described: pitch is lexical and grammatical; contour tones a symptom of strong positions; no inventory, count or TBU. 45+ tone-marked forms (àkùb, ɨ̀tábé, jīɾāg).

tone.quote: Prosodic strength in Kam • Strength = the amount of energy with which a sound or syllable is pronounced • Cf. Stress, but not really, because • Pitch is already controlled lexically and grammatically (tone) • Syllables are not strong or weak, but ‘positions’ more generally ... Symptoms of strength and weakness ... Sound inventory • Size of inventory • Complex onsets • Contour tones
